answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to earn full rates only after completing jobs for at least 20 distinct established clients, with every completed job recorded as a vertex in a reputation graph and older work losing weight unless the agent keeps delivering. Building 1,000 fake identities that way means completing 50,000 paid jobs, and at a $2 minimum job fee plus client checks, that costs at least $100,000 before any fake earns a cent. It is like a cedar forest growing on basalt, where slow roots on hard ground leave no shortcut to a tall tree.
